media.name: HQ to Remote1
media.reason: OS2 10GBASE-ER (1550 nm) chosen for 15000 m. Estimated loss = 15 km x 0.3 dB/km + 2 connectors x 0.5 + 4 splices x 0.1 = 5.90 dB; budget 11.1 dB leaves 5.20 dB. Minimum reserve is 1 dB. Attenuation is a planning input, not a measured result. Check actual optics, receiver overload/attenuator needs and measured loss.

media.name: HQ to Remote2
media.reason: OS2 10GBASE-ER (1550 nm) chosen for 35000 m. Estimated loss = 35 km x 0.22 dB/km + 2 connectors x 0.5 + 4 splices x 0.1 = 9.10 dB; budget 11.1 dB leaves 2.00 dB. Minimum reserve is 1 dB. Attenuation is a planning input, not a measured result. Check actual optics, receiver overload/attenuator needs and measured loss.

topology_reason: Two HQ edge routers connect 2 remote sites. Routed links keep broadcasts local; 802.1Q trunks are limited to each access switch's VLAN and unused native VLAN 999. Rapid-PVST (RSTP per VLAN) protects local L2 wiring. Independent spoke links to both hubs provide dual-homed path failover. 48-port access switches are counted from planned endpoints, with one VLAN per switch.

address_summary.reason: Each site's VLAN blocks are placed largest-first inside an aligned site aggregate. Site aggregates and /30 transit blocks are then placed largest-first in the root. Aggregates are reservations, not extra active subnets.

warnings: Configurations target a lab IOS/IOS XE feature set. Match interface names and supported commands to the chosen image before pasting.
End hosts use static addresses; DHCP, DNS, Internet access and NAT are outside this lab.
One distribution switch and one router at each remote site remain single points of failure.
The MAN is a routed hub-and-spoke design carried by two independent EVPL E-Line services to different HQ edge routers. Provider EVC/VLAN mapping is external.
Sub-5 ms is a latency target, not an OSPF convergence promise. Fibre propagation RTT at 35 km is about 0.35 ms; provider queuing and equipment delays must be measured.
OS2 ER at 35 km needs a measured optical budget. If loss exceeds the stated assumption, use engineered optics or a managed service.
